skill.name: allra-test-writing
skill.description: Standards for writing Allra Java backend tests with JUnit 5, Spring Boot, AssertJ, Mockito, Fixture Monkey, and project test helpers.

content.value_statement: Backend teams need consistent test scope, structure, data, and assertions. This skill guides Allra Java tests using established helpers and testing libraries.
actual_capabilities: Selects Allra test helpers based on component type and required test scope.
Explains when to use mocked unit tests, repository tests, controller tests, or integration tests.
Applies Given-When-Then structure with JUnit 5, AssertJ, and Mockito.
Shows Fixture Monkey patterns for creating controlled Java test data.
Provides examples for controller, service, repository, transaction, event, and workflow tests.
Documents Gradle and Maven test commands with a quality checklist.
limitations: The guidance targets Java 17 and Spring Boot 3.2 or later.
Allra helper classes may be unavailable in projects outside the standard template.
The skill does not execute tests or measure coverage by itself.
Dependency versions and examples may require adjustment for each project.

use_cases.title: Choose a test scope
use_cases.description: Identify the lightest suitable Allra test helper for a new service, controller, repository, or workflow.

use_cases.title: Standardize a test suite
use_cases.description: Align test naming, structure, assertions, mocks, fixtures, and coverage expectations across a Java codebase.

use_cases.title: Review financial workflows
use_cases.description: Check that payment, rollback, database integrity, and state transition tests use appropriate integration coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a helper
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the Allra test helper for this component and explain the decision: [component and behavior].
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a clear test scope recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a unit test
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a JUnit 5 test for [method]. Use Given-When-Then, AssertJ, Mockito, and the Allra naming convention.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a focused service or domain test.

prompt_templates.title: Design integration coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design tests for [workflow]. Cover transactions, database consistency, state changes, and events. Mock every external system.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan coverage for a multi-step backend workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an existing suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Review tests in [scope] against Allra standards. Identify incorrect helpers, missing scenarios, weak assertions, unnecessary integration tests, and nondeterministic data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform an advanced suite-level quality review.

output_examples.input: Choose a test type for a service that calculates a discount using one repository.
output_examples.output: Use MockingUnitTest. Mock the repository, inject the service, and verify the calculation and repository interaction.

output_examples.input: Plan tests for a payment workflow that updates three tables and must roll back on failure.
output_examples.output: Use IntegrationTest for database consistency and rollback behavior. Mock the payment gateway and verify both success and failure states.

output_examples.input: Review a controller test that starts the full Spring application.
output_examples.output: Replace the full context with ControllerTest or WebMvcTest. Mock the service and assert status, response fields, and validation failures.

best_practices: Use the lightest test helper that verifies the required behavior.
Structure every test with explicit Given, When, and Then phases.
Mock external systems while verifying internal database and transaction behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not use IntegrationTest for simple calculations or single-entity service logic.
Do not call payment gateways, notification services, or other external APIs from tests.
Do not rely on random fixture values when a scenario requires specific fields.

faq.question: When should I use IntegrationTest?
faq.answer: Use it for financial transactions, rollback behavior, multiple-table consistency, database constraints, complex state changes, events, or several collaborating services.

faq.question: What should I use for ordinary service logic?
faq.answer: Use MockingUnitTest with Mockito for calculations, validation, transformations, simple queries, and single-entity operations.

faq.question: Can I use standard Spring test annotations?
faq.answer: Yes. Use standard Spring Boot annotations when Allra helper classes are unavailable, while keeping the same scope and structure principles.

faq.question: How should external integrations be tested?
faq.answer: Mock external gateways, APIs, and notification services. Integration tests should focus on internal transactions and data consistency.

faq.question: Is Fixture Monkey required?
faq.answer: No. It is optional and useful for fixture creation, but scenario-critical fields should be set explicitly.

faq.question: Does this skill run the tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and commands, but the agent or developer must run tests in the project environment.
